h: Petrol falls to ₦1,055 at Lagos depots as MRS cuts pump price
p: Five Lagos depots cut their petrol price to ₦1,055 per litre on Tuesday, the lowest among surveyed terminals. MRS stations in Abuja have reduced their pump price by ₦70 to ₦1,295.
body: Petrol prices have fallen further in Nigeria's wholesale market as competition among depot operators intensifies.
Five Lagos-based depots cut their ex-depot price of petrol to ₦1,055 per litre on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, the lowest rate among the terminals surveyed by a market tracker.
The cuts are slowly reaching filling stations. MRS stations in Abuja reduced their pump price by ₦70 to ₦1,295 per litre, although that is still well above the depot rate.
Prices have been falling for several weeks amid competition between Dangote Refinery and fuel importers, though motorists have complained that pump prices are slow to reflect lower wholesale rates.
MRS has also cut its pump price by ₦70 in Lagos, following Dangote Refinery's recent ₦99 cut.
more: Five Lagos depots now sell at ₦1,055.
MRS cut its Abuja pump price to ₦1,295.
Pump prices are still well above depot rates.
